title: Joining Eugene Coy's Happy Black Aces and the trip to Amarillo
summary: After graduating in 1928, Budd and Keg join Eugene Coy in Shawnee, whose job ends and band drives through blowouts to Amarillo.

bands.name: Eugene Coy and His Happy Black Aces

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: All right, now my class was 1928, and I finished high school. And after I finished high school my brother and I -- this was early -- had a call to join Eugene Coy and his Happy Black Aces. They called for us to come to Shawnee, Oklahoma. That's where the Blackfoot Indians are. I used to hang out on these reservations and drink that Choctaw beer with
these Indians, you know, like -- but --

And so we left. We left home together, and we joined Eugene Coy. Now they had been working at a beautiful ballroom. You know, they had ballrooms and all in those days, where they played strictly for dancing?

Well when my brother and I got there we played about days and the contract was over. The job ended. And I said what is this? So the guy say, Eugene Coy, he says well don't worry about it. He says we're going to Amarillo, Texas. That's my home town, and we'll get further work there. And says my mother and father's there, and everything. He says so don't worry about a thing.

All right, so he had this one car, and incidentally, Eddie Durham's brothers played in the band, one on bass and one on trombone. And I'm very embarassed at this point that I can't remember their first names. I think -- I think one's name was Clyde, and I don't remember the other's name. Good musicians, like Eddy. And so we went in to Amarillo, Texas, and on the way, driving from Shawnee, Oklahoma to Amarillo, Texas we must have had about 13 or 14 blowouts, because all of this weight in this one car, with all of our instruments, and suitcases, and we would stop at the filling station and leave a little security and get an old tire and ride a little farther, a blowout, and blowout, we were riding all on the fenders, and the running boards and everything. And it was in

the wintertime.
So when we arrived in Amarillo, Texas it was 15 below zero! Can you imagine that? Up in the Panhandle. 15 below zero! And so when we got there Eugene Coy was really in his hometown, so he took as many people as he could to his parent's home, and the rest of us he put us up in a little hotel over a drugstore there. It was like what you may call like a shopping center, was about like a square block. They had a theater, and a hotel, a laundry, and whatnot.
